title: Employee Messages to Administrator Trigger Zero In-App Notifications and Zero Push Notifications
problem:
CRITICAL NOTIFICATION FLAW: When an employee sends a direct or team message to an administrator, the server returns HTTP 201 'Message sent.' but COMPLETELY FAILS to generate any in-app notification record or dispatch any FCM push notification to the administrator.

Live Production Verification:
1. Super Admin (user_id=1, dragon@bingi.com.bd) registered an active Android FCM push device token (device_id=16) via POST /push-devices.
2. Employee Yeapas (user_id=66, employee_id=2) sent a message to the administrator via POST /messages/1/send. Server responded HTTP 201.
3. Querying GET /notifications for Super Admin returned ZERO new notification entries (unread_count remained unchanged at 107; no notification row inserted).
4. Querying GET /push-deliveries confirmed that NO FCM push delivery was ever queued, recorded, or dispatched to user_id=1.
5. In reverse: When Super Admin sent a message to the employee in the exact same conversation, the server successfully created in-app notification id 25879 ('New message from Super Admin') and triggered push delivery.

Root Cause Analysis:
• Super Admin has user_id=1, role=SUPER_ADMIN, but has NO record in the 'employees' database table (employee.id is 0 or null). POST /messages rejects Admin recipients with HTTP 422 ('The selected recipient employee id is invalid.' / 'Select a staff recipient.').
• When a message is sent, the backend notification dispatcher resolves recipients strictly by looking up conversation_participants.employee_id and mapping to employees.user_id. Because the administrator is not an employee row in the participants table, the listener completely skips user_id=1.
expected:
1. Update POST /team-operations/messages to accept direct conversation creation with administrators via recipient_user_id (e.g. 1 / 'usr_1').
2. In the message sending controller / event listener (e.g. ConversationMessageController@send), resolve conversation participants by user_id in addition to employee_id.
3. When any employee sends a message in a conversation involving an administrator (or team chat supervised by admin), create an in-app notification record in the 'notifications' table for user_id=1 with type='message', entity.type='team_conversation', and data.event='message_received'.
4. Dispatch an FCM push notification payload to all registered device tokens for user_id=1 via Firebase Cloud Messaging.

title: Follow-Up Due Reminders and Overdue Alerts Are Dispatched ONLY to Admin (Assigned Employee Receives Zero Alerts)
problem:
CRITICAL WORKFLOW FLAW: When a follow-up is scheduled with a reminder (e.g. 15 minutes before due time) or when a follow-up becomes overdue, the backend background reminder daemon triggers notification cards and FCM push notifications ONLY to Super Admin (user_id=1). The employee to whom the follow-up is assigned receives ZERO in-app notifications and ZERO push notifications.

Live Production Verification & Evidence:
1. Follow-up #25 ('Sea Pearl Beach Resort & Spa') was created with assignee_employee_id=2 (Yeapas / user_id=66), scheduled for 5:44 PM.
2. When the 15-minute reminder fired (17:28:00), the server created in-app notification #14398 ('Follow-up due in 15 minutes') and push delivery #122 exclusively for user_id=1 (Super Admin).
3. When the follow-up became overdue (17:45:01), the server created notification #14470 ('Followup overdue') and push delivery #123 exclusively for user_id=1 (Super Admin).
4. Querying the employee's inbox (GET /notifications) confirmed that the employee received the initial creation card (#14006), but received ZERO reminder cards and ZERO overdue cards.
5. Querying GET /push-deliveries confirmed that 100% of all 87 push dispatches across the entire backend database were targeted to user_id=1. Zero push dispatches exist for any assigned staff employee.
expected:
In the background scheduler / cron worker that checks scheduled follow-ups (and tasks/visits):
1. Resolve the assigned employee (followup.assignee_employee_id) and map to their linked user account (e.g. User::where('employee_id', $followup->assignee_employee_id)->first()).
2. Insert the 'followups.reminder' and 'followups.overdue' notification rows into the 'notifications' table for the ASSIGNED EMPLOYEE's user_id so it appears in their in-app notification inbox.
3. Dispatch the FCM push notification to all active device tokens registered by the ASSIGNED EMPLOYEE in 'push_devices'.
4. While alerting administrators is useful as a supervisory rollup, the primary assignee MUST receive both the in-app notification and FCM push alert.

title: Employee Certificates & Testimonials Request, Moderation & Delivery (100% Missing Backend API)

problem:
COMPLETE LIFECYCLE FEATURE CONTRACT MISSING:
When an employee leaves the company or requires verified proof of service (e.g. for higher studies, visa applications, or new career opportunities), they require an official Work Experience Certificate, Testimonial, or Relieving Letter.

The mobile app has implemented the complete end-to-end lifecycle:
1. Employee Request Submission: From the 'More' menu in Profile, employees can request a certificate by selecting Type ('Work Experience Certificate', 'Testimonial', 'Relieving Letter'), specifying Purpose ('Higher Education', 'New Employment', 'Visa / Immigration', 'General'), and providing additional notes.
2. Real-time Status Tracking: The employee can track request states: 'Pending Approval', 'In Preparation', 'Delivered', or 'Rejected'.
3. Admin Management Dashboard: Administrators access 'Certificates & Testimonials' from More > Work Operations with filter chips for All, Pending Approval, In Preparation, Delivered, and Rejected.
4. Moderation Workflow: Admin can Accept or Reject requests. Rejection requires a mandatory reason and sends an immediate alert to the employee.
5. Certificate Template & Issuance: For accepted requests, the Admin fills the official issuance template with Certificate Number (e.g. 'NEC-CERT-2026-0042'), Conduct Assessment ('Exceptional', 'Excellent', 'Good', 'Satisfactory'), Key Contributions, Authorized Signatory Name & Designation (e.g. 'Nazmul Hasan - CEO & Founder'), and Issue Date.
6. Official PDF Generation & Delivery: The system generates an official PDF document with company letterhead, official seal, and signature, sets the status to 'Delivered', and sends an in-app and push notification to the employee.

BACKEND DEFICIENCY:
The backend currently has ZERO endpoints for certificate management (all return HTTP 404). This entire module runs in mock state.
